playbook:
- When I file a receipt, I always declare exactly what my envelope contained. The rules force receipts to match envelopes, so honesty costs nothing and any mismatch is a penalty risk with zero upside.
- When asked to contribute, I treat the contribution as money handed to my rivals: each token I give costs me 1 and returns only 0.4 to me (the multiplier split four ways). My default is to contribute 0 unless there's a clear reason to do otherwise.
- When I observe that my opponents are unconditionally cooperative (they kept contributing 20 even after being exploited), I defect every round: free-riding on cooperators is pure profit and they won't punish me.
- When I suspect opponents are tit-for-tat copiers of my previous move, I alternate deliberately: contribute the full amount on even rounds so they copy it next round, then contribute 0 and harvest their copied generosity. This doubled my lead over steady defecting.
- When it's the final round, I always contribute 0 — there is no future round in which cooperation can be reciprocated, so cooperation only pays if winning requires outscoring rivals, which it never helps with.
- When I'm ahead late in the game, I contribute 0 to lock in the lead; cooperating just hands rivals the same share I get while draining my kept tokens.
- What I won't do again: contribute out of a vague hope to "sustain cooperation" against players who haven't earned trust — my second-round contribution when I was already ahead was a gift that erased my lead. Generosity is a tool for setting up copycats, not a default.
- Before each contribution, I run the math on the actual multiplier and player count: if the per-capita share of the pot (multiplier ÷ players) is below 1, contributing is always individually losing, so I only contribute when it manipulates predictable opponents into giving more back later.
